angerschateau.name: Angers Castle
angerschateau.slogan: Seventeen dark towers guarding a tapestry of the end of the world.
angerschateau.line: Its 660-metre wall, three metres thick, is studded with seventeen towers; the Apocalypse Tapestry was ordered in 1373.

fontevraudabbey.name: Fontevraud Abbey
fontevraudabbey.slogan: The abbey where Eleanor of Aquitaine and Richard the Lionheart lie.
fontevraudabbey.line: Founded in 1101 by the wandering preacher Robert of Arbrissel, it counted some 3,000 nuns by his death in 1117.

saumurchateau.name: Château de Saumur
saumurchateau.slogan: The fairy-tale fortress above the Loire, straight from a medieval calendar.
saumurchateau.line: It appears on the September page of the Très Riches Heures du duc de Berry, as it looked in 1410.

brissacchateau.name: Château de Brissac
brissacchateau.slogan: Seven storeys of Loire Valley height, with a gilded theatre inside.
brissacchateau.line: At seven storeys it is the tallest château in France, and Louis XIII met his mother Marie de Medici here in 1620.

angerscathedral.name: Angers Cathedral
angerscathedral.slogan: Twelfth-century glass still glowing high above the Maine.
angerscathedral.line: Its Childhood of Christ window, given between 1163 and 1177, holds the cathedral's oldest stained glass.
